title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class parallel Pollard rho in GT with a cyclotomic-squaring branch, success target 0.39

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with M=2^20 walks, R=1024 partitions and theta=2^-60) succeeds with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.612 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000). The walk mixes two step types on the class space: with probability s=35/64 (a fixed 6-bit field of T0=Re(c_0), equal on all 12 conjugates and costing no multiplication) the step is y<-y^2 by cyclotomic squaring, valid on GT and commuting with Frobenius, with exponents (alpha,beta)<-(2alpha,2beta) mod r; otherwise it is one twisted-table multiplication y<-y*T[h][t] with the twelve conjugate keys computed from four Fp multiplications, the partition h taken from ten bits of T0 and the twist t from kappa, as in the published Frobenius-class design. The three per-step decision fields (partition bits 0..9, branch bits 10..15, distinguished bits 16..75 of T0) are disjoint bit ranges of one class invariant, so outside cycle handling every step is a function of the current class and two walks at one class take the same step, while the two cycle escapes are functions of the cycle reached, not of the walker (the 2-cycle escape squares the smaller-T0 class, the checkpoint escape walks to the cycle's smallest-T0 class and squares it), so two walks that reach one cycle compute the same escape class and action and follow the same class sequence from their first common class, while their DETECTION times can differ by up to one 64-step checkpoint period plus the cycle length (<= 128 steps, charged); a squaring step computes no class key, and the 128-bit report key is derived from the class key K, computed at a report and charged there. Every per-step decision, the class-key ORDERING that defines kappa and the report slice are read from the Montgomery-domain values the blst kernels produce, no canonical conversion charged: the twelve keys are compared as key*R mod p, so kappa, the canonical representative and each twist are the ones that ordering selects, and the report key is bits 70..197 of that Montgomery-ordered minimum K. K is a minimum of twelve keys, so it is not a uniform Fp element, and the package claims no uniform-bits preservation: those 128 bits are taken as pseudo-random under H1, with part A2's frequencies as evidence. The 2-cycle and checkpoint comparisons run every step and compare T0 (381 bits; a false match has probability about 2^-380.70, total below 2^-253, and can only cause a spurious escape, never a false logarithm). The squaring step is measured, not modelled: blst's blst_fp12_cyclotomic_sqr at revision f7a88067 costs 9,803.0 executed instructions per call ((I65-I1)/64) on the COST_MODEL toolchain, identical at five offsets; measure/ ships the records and experiment.py re-derives the price; the ledger charges the body 9,798. The charge is 10,098 instructions = 0.50490 units (9,798 plus 300 for the doubling, shared rows and slack); with that price the W-minimising branch fraction is s=35/64,. Collision law: squaring is injective on classes (|GT| is odd) so squaring-squaring pairs never merge, squaring-multiply pairs merge at about 1/N, and multiply-multiply pairs at about (1-1/(12R))/N, giving N'=N/(1-s^2-(1-s)^2/R)=2^251.785203, charged with 1/R instead of 1/(12R) in the third term (N' larger by 3.78 x 10^-4 in log2), S0'=sqrt(2N'ln(1/0.61))=2^125.884326 and S=1.05 S0'=2^125.954715 steps. Fruitless cycles are all-multiply only: with t>=1 squaring steps the exponent pair gains 2^t p^m, which is 1 mod r only when ord_r(2)=(r-1)/16=2^250.857 divides 12t, i.e. t>=2^247.27, so their rates carry (1-s)^L (0.0101 R^-2 for L=3..64 against 0.1391 R^-2 unbranched) and the ledger charges the unbranched R^-2 at 200 steps. Within-walk returns are escaped, useful, or a wasted slot: fruitless 2-cycles (rate (1-s)^2/(12R)=1.671 x 10^-5 per step) and checkpoint cycles of length 3..64 are detected and escaped inside the charge, and a revisit with a different exponent pair is the useful collision. More generally a slot's walk can meet its own class (probability at most n^2/(2N')=2^-40.875 per slot for n=2^105.955 steps) and spend the rest of its budget on repeats: it wastes at most its remaining n steps, its meter stops it at W_cap, the work bound is unchanged, and the success loss is at most 2^-21.62 (2^-20.96 of S except with probability below 2^-19.91 by Markov), beside the older 2^-19 self-collision term. The log's capacity rests on the deterministic per-slot cap R_w=2^47, C_rep=M R_w=2^67, not on returns. Because the branch bit is a function of the class, step costs are not i.i.d. across time, so the slot's work is accounted by type: productive steps on newly exposed classes take i.i.d. costs in [0.50490, 1.1125] with mean 0.78021875 (H1 supplies a fresh draw there), the 2^80-step per-slot allowance inside W_cap covers ordinary revisits, and cycle handling is charged the declared allowance. The meter is a private 128-bit instruction counter with hard cap W_cap=2^119.899627, so all walk work is at most M x (W_cap-1+20,000+2,250+3,000)=2^125.611915 units as a deterministic bound; Hoeffding at a=10^-5 bounds productive work above (1+a) of nominal by 2^(-2^74.98) per slot (2^(-2^94.98) over the run; exponents of the exponent) under H1's fresh-class law, so productive work is bounded except with probability below 2^-100; the 1% band is split once, a slot aborting only on that event or on cycle work above its allowance plus the band 0.01 nominal + 2^80 steps less a of productive nominal (2^98.80 steps): P(cycle work > band) <= 2^91.73/2^98.80 = 2^-7.07 per slot by Markov on the H1 mean, charged 0.00745 inside the 0.01 allowance, a stopped slot being charged as if it stored no DP; the nominal charges a deterministic allowance, 1.000435 x S at the multiply-step price, 8.35 times its H1 mean rate, and the same meter charges every cycle step, so the work bound holds whatever the count is. The 0.01 allowance is slack for the model's heuristic parts. The report machinery is direct-addressed: a log of exactly M R_w = 2^67 records of 80 bytes, an append rule that stores no repeat of the walk's last record after both cycle checks, a per-slot cumulative DP-ATTEMPT counter, incremented by every distinguished hit stored or suppressed, carried across restarts and stopping the slot at R_w, each attempt charged 3,000 instructions to the slot's meter, matched offline by an in-place heapsort of the whole 80-byte record (budgeted 10,000) with one adjacent 80-byte comparison per record for duplicate removal and at most one 200-instruction charge per pair in an equal-key run, against a hard pair budget P=2^41 whose abort probability is at most 2^-36 by Markov; the first pair of equal canonical elements with different exponent pairs gives x=(A1-A2)/(B2-B1) mod r and the output is verified by e(P,Q)=z. Peak memory is below 2^73.4 bytes (a hard bound: 2^67 records of 80 bytes plus table and walk states, no hashing or eviction); preprocessing and table construction are at most 2^57 group-operation equivalents, including the 2^56.30-unit initialization of all 2^67 log records, all included in W; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound is 0.42013 (model at 1.05 S0', rounded down) minus the 0.01 allowance minus 2^-18 of loss terms >= 0.41012 >= 0.39 (the toys pool 0.4080 +- 0.0090 at that budget, 0.971 of the model, 0.3980 after the same allowance), and rests on the standard random-mapping heuristic for the mixed walk (branch-adjusted Brent-Pollard correction, 5% step slack), the same heuristic behind the cycle allowance and the report-cap margin (mean 2^45.955 attempts per slot, cap 2^47); toy-field experiments run the production fields from T0, squaring, step order, append rule, meter and matcher, and the branch-adjusted collision law is measured directly; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements, check GT membership, the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula and its distinctness, that the two-subtraction sign-set minimum equals the twelve-way argmin and class key, that kappa selects the same canonical representative from all 12 conjugates, p^6 = inversion, ord_r(p) = 12, the factorisation of r-1 and ord_r(2) = (r-1)/16 with the smallest t that a fruitless cycle could contain, that T0 = Re(c_0) is equal on all 12 conjugates of the Montgomery value, and that the measured cyclotomic-squaring routine equals y*y on GT. Part A2: frequencies of the 76 used bits of the Montgomery value of T0 (partition, branch and distinguished fields) and of the 128 report-key bits, bits 70..197 of the Montgomery-ordered class key K (the twelve keys formed as key*R mod p and minimised in that form), on real GT elements, plus the measured branch-field and distinguished-field fractions. Every per-step decision, the key ordering and the report slice are read from the Montgomery-domain values the kernels hold (T0*2^384 mod p and the same form of K). Part P: the production step rule on real GT elements with a 16-entry table and kappa taken from the Montgomery keys, two walkers started at two different conjugates of one element, which must produce the same T0 sequence, with the exponent invariant y = g^alpha z^beta checked for both and the squaring fraction, multiply steps, reports and key computations counted. Part E: the branch-adjusted collision law measured directly in the toy field q = 67 by sampling distinct classes, applying one step to each and counting image coincidences by pair type, compared with 1 - s^2 - (1-s)^2/(12R) and with the charged 1 - s^2 - (1-s)^2/R, with squaring-squaring coincidences required to be exactly zero. Part B: the complete mixed walk (T0 bit fields, Granger-Scott squaring, four-multiplication keys only on multiply steps with kappa taken from the toy field's Montgomery form, the 2-cycle escape and the checkpoint escape that traverses the cycle to its smallest-T0 class and squares it, stuck-walk rule, append rule, per-slot DP-attempt cap (every distinguished hit counted and charged), per-slot work meter) in three toy fields near 2^20 with the production step order, every trial run to the fixed step budget 1.05 S0', then the production offline matcher (full 80-byte-record sort, adjacent dedup, charged equal-key pairs against a hard pair budget, element recomputation, exponentiation check), with stress passes for the DP-attempt cap, the stuck-walk restart with the carried slot counter, the work meter and the pair budget. Part C: the bound arithmetic of proof.md, including the zero-sum probabilities, the fruitless-cycle rates with and without the branch, the measured cyclotomic-squaring price against the counted rows, the branch fraction, N', S0', the deterministic report-log capacity, the KL report-cap margin, the memory bound, the per-record report charge, the hard pair budget, the work-meter cap as an exact integer, its Hoeffding concentration exponent, the cycle allowance carried as a declared allowance rather than a tail bound, the counter-width table, and an exact integer check that the claim is log2 W rounded up at three decimals. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs or production key statistics.
